# Stories into tests

A story is what someone wants checked, in their words: a file in `stories/new/`, with its acceptance criteria.

- `crew`, then "Turn the new stories into tests" (or `claude`, then `/stories`): Claude Code writes a test for
  each criterion, in the suite's own page objects and words, and runs it.
- A story it cannot test as written comes back with a question (a push-back) in its file. Answer under it, on a
  line starting `Answer:`, and run it again.
- A story whose tests pass moves to `stories/done/`, with a note naming each criterion's test.

Stories can come from Jira: `jira login` once, then `jira pull` brings the ready ones in, and `jira push` sends each
card its tests or its questions (`jira-loop/README.md`).

## Who the crew runs as

- **In a pipeline** the crew is its own job and holds the AI's key alone; the Jira token and the token that publishes are
  in the other jobs, never in its. On GitLab a CI/CD variable reaches every job unless it is scoped to an environment:
  scope `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to the environment `crew`, and the Jira and push tokens to `jira`, so the suite's other jobs
  are given none of them.
- **As its own user.** Inside the crew's job, `jira-loop/stories.sh` makes a user `crew` (it must run as root, or as a
  user with passwordless `sudo`: a disposable runner or container), gives it the checkout, and runs everything of the
  crew's (the dependency fetch, the AI, the checks it starts) as that user, with an environment of named variables only:
  the AI's key, `PATH`, `JAVA_HOME`, the proxy variables and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, nothing else. The job token the
  runner holds in its own processes cannot be read by another user. When the crew is done, the script kills every
  process of the crew, puts `.git` back as it was before the crew started, and copies only plain `*.bundle` files into
  `jira-loop/run/upload/`, the one folder the pipeline uploads. Without root or `sudo` it refuses; set
  `SUITE_CREW_SAME_USER=1` to run the crew as the job's own user anyway. It then can read what that user can read,
  including the job's token in its parent processes' environment, and the script says so.
- **What the crew does not get from the runner.** The crew has a home folder of its own, so a Maven mirror or login in the
  runner's `~/.m2/settings.xml` does not reach it. Give it one on purpose: in a step before `stories.sh`, create the
  user (`sudo useradd --create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin crew`) and write the settings file for it
  (`sudo install -D -o crew -m 600 settings.xml /home/crew/.m2/settings.xml`). The script reuses a `crew` that is in no
  other group and has no `sudo`. Whatever you put there the AI can read, so give it a read-only login for the mirror, and
  give the proxy variables an address without a login in it.
- **What the publish step refuses.** The crew's bundle is data to the job that publishes it, because that job holds the push
  token and Jira's. It reads the bundle in a repository of its own, never checked out, with no hooks. It refuses a bundle that
  `git bundle verify` or `git fsck` rejects, that is over 20 MB or takes git more than two minutes to read, or that is
  not named for its own agent (`bundle-<agent>/<agent>.bundle`); a ref other than `refs/heads/stories/<card>` for a card
  this agent was given; a branch that adds more than 20000 objects, or was not started from the commit the run claimed, or
  differs from main in a file the pipeline runs;
  a branch with a file over 5 MB, a path outside the folder (absolute, `..`, or a name Windows or macOS would read as `.git`,
  or a `.gitmodules` link); and a branch that changes what the pipeline runs: `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-*.yml`, `.github/`,
  `jira-loop/`, `.mvn/`, `pom.xml`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `.npmrc`, `cypress.config.*`, `tsconfig.json`,
  `Dockerfile`, `.claude/`, `.vscode/` and any `.git*` name. A refused card goes back in the queue with a comment naming the
  file or the ref, and nothing of it is pushed; if the change is one you want, make it yourself in a pull request. A branch
  is pushed over the one the run last saw (`--force-with-lease`), so a person's later commit on it is never overwritten.
- **On your computer** the crew runs as you. The menu starts Claude Code with `secrets/` denied to its file reads
  (`--disallowedTools "Read(./secrets/**)"`). That is a partial guard: what you can read in a shell, a command it runs
  can read too. Keep nothing in this folder that you would not give the AI.
